prototype.name: dd_flow_300s
prototype.mechanism: Drawdown-state conditioning of accumulated flow: the distance of mid from its running intraday high measures trapped-long / stop-loss potential energy. Directional flow delivered WHILE the instrument sits deep below its day-high is more informative: distressed selling, stop cascades and opportunistic absorption all concentrate in that state, so the same accumulated imbalance carries different implications at the high vs in the drawdown. value = (trailing-300s mean trade imbalance) x (-drawdown), amplifying accumulated flow by drawdown depth. Neither component alone (imbalance accumulation, price position) captures the interaction. Whether the sign of IC comes out continuation (selling begets selling) or absorption (dip-buying reverses) is the empirical question; the screen is two-sided.
prototype.inspiration: Lens item 'drawdown-from-day-open interactions'; digest iter-000 coverage GAP: price-position/time-of-day information unused by all 12 library factors; intraday-extreme anchoring (George & Hwang 2004) adapted to the running day-high; stop-cascade / distress continuation vs absorption is a standard minutes-scale regime mechanism.

prototype.name: depth5_delta_60s
prototype.mechanism: Depth delta: the trailing-60s CHANGE in 5-level depth imbalance (bid-ask)/(bid+ask), not its level. A book whose bid-side depth stock is actively growing relative to the ask side is experiencing net limit-order inflow on the bid - latent demand building up before it shows up in trades. The level of imbalance (wdi) is crowded and slow; the delta captures the flow INTO the deeper book and should decorrelate from the level by construction (differencing removes the persistent state), targeting the digest's explicitly unexplored 'depth delta' dimension.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000 opportunity map: 'Depth-side unexplored: resiliency, depth delta, queue position, large-order depth share'; cross-family mutation away from the depth mega-family has higher marginal value (rho 0.69 within family); Cao-Hansch-Wang (2009) information content of the book's depth dynamics.

prototype.name: depth_resiliency
prototype.mechanism: Depth resiliency: market makers with quoting obligations replenish the book after trades consume it. The 60s change in TOTAL depth (bid+ask), normalized by its trailing 300s level, is a snapshot resiliency proxy. Rising total depth = active replenishment, so recent shocks are transient (mean reversion); falling total depth = liquidity withdrawal, so shocks are informative (continuation). Built from total depth, NOT bid-vs-ask imbalance, so it sits in a different dimension from the wdi/oir/microprice mega-family.
prototype.inspiration: digest: 'Depth-side unexplored: resiliency, depth delta, queue position, large-order depth share'; Foucault-Kadan-Kandel (2005) and Obizhaeva-Wang (2013) resiliency -> reversal-vs-continuation over 1-5 minutes (targets the open 300s horizon).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: flow_divergence_300s
prototype.mechanism: Absorption / stealth limit flow: the trailing-300s z-score of OFI (order-book-delta flow: limit placement/pull at the touch) minus the z-score of executed trade imbalance. Positive divergence means the book is being built on the bid side relative to what aggressive trades justify - passive buyers absorbing sell aggression (iceberg/stealth accumulation); negative divergence is the mirror. The limit-flow component dominates for next-move prediction (CKS: OFI R2 > signed volume), and disagreement between executed and book-building flow flags informed traders hiding in the book, so the divergence direction should carry into 15s-300s returns.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: ofi vs trade_imbalance rho=0.49 and 'the ORDER-BOOK-DELTA component of OFI not in trade imbalance is worth isolating'; Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov (2014) OFI dominates signed volume; absorption via iceberg orders (Buti & Rindi 2013, undisplayed liquidity).

prototype.name: iopv_premium_mom
prototype.mechanism: IOPV premium momentum: the exchange IOPV refreshes on <=15s steps while the ETF trades continuously, so the premium's 30s rate of change is distinct from its level. A widening premium (ETF running ahead of fair value) flags continuation pressure; a narrowing premium flags active arbitrage pull-back. This is the lead-lag between basket fair value and ETF price captured as premium velocity, not premium level.
prototype.inspiration: digest: 'IOPV dimension is thin (1 factor, level only); premium momentum/delta ... unexplored and orthogonal to the depth mega-family' (max |rho| of iopv_premium vs all others = 0.23); docs/knowledge/02 ETF lead-lag section (basket/fair-value pulls the ETF with seconds-to-minutes lag).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: large_trade_share_level
prototype.mechanism: Size-distribution level: a rising share of volume in large trades flags informed/institutional activity (stealth accumulation splits small orders, aggressive information events do not). Unlike ofi / trade_imbalance (signed net flow) this measures WHO is trading, not the net direction; on 15-60s horizons a burst of large prints typically precedes continuation of the just-revealed move, on 300-900s it marks regime episodes. Direction-free by construction -- the sign comes from the concurrent price/flow columns if the IC is signed, otherwise the factor works via its own rank ordering.
prototype.inspiration: iter-001 candidates.json needs_materialization entry (accumulation-regime lens): trade-size distribution was untestable on the 12-column panel; digest: 'large prints concentrate information'. Zhang & Shen (2018, trade-size decomposition of price impact); Bouchaud et al. 2009 (anomalous impact of large trades).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: ofi_accum_300s
prototype.mechanism: Accumulated order-book-delta pressure over minutes: the engine's ofi_60s is the Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov best-quote OFI (limit-order placements, pulls AND trades) normalized by mean best depth, and its IC decays from 0.093@15s to ~0 by 900s. But OFI's price impact relaxes only as a power law, so successive minutes of net-positive queue building leave residual pressure that a 60s window forgets. Averaging OFI over 300s yields a minutes-scale accumulation state distinct from both trade-flow accumulation (digest rho(ofi, trade_imbalance) = 0.49, only partial overlap) and static book levels (wdi/oir). Targets 300s/900s.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'the ORDER-BOOK-DELTA component of OFI not in trade imbalance is worth isolating'; Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) OFI linear impact; Bouchaud et al. (2004) propagator t^-1/2 tail justifies multi-minute integration of flow; 300s horizon is the weakest-and-most-open gap (mean |IC| 0.064, 0/12 stage1 passes).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: prem_x_ofi
prototype.mechanism: Premium x order-flow interaction: premium mean-reversion is driven by AP creation/redemption arbitrage, but its speed depends on the prevailing order flow. When the ETF is at a premium AND net order flow is selling, the forces reinforce reversion (stronger predicted down-move); when flow opposes the premium, reversion is delayed. The product of the causally z-scored premium and OFI isolates this conditional-reversion channel rather than either signal alone.
prototype.inspiration: digest: 'premium x order-flow interaction ... orthogonal to the depth mega-family'; iopv_premium is the strongest mean-reversion signal (|t|=7.9) and ofi_60s the strongest flow signal, yet their INTERACTION is unexplored and sits in a different info dimension.

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: prem_x_wdi
prototype.mechanism: Premium x depth-imbalance interaction: a positive premium means the ETF is rich vs fair value (arbitrage pressure downward), but the book's depth imbalance decides how fast reversion lands. A premium paired with a bid-heavy book (high wdi) is being propped up and reverts slowly; paired with an ask-heavy book it snaps back fast. The product of causally z-scored premium and wdi captures this conditional-reversion timing, a cross-family interaction.
prototype.inspiration: digest: wdi is the cost-friendly champion (slowest decay, half-life 900s) and iopv_premium the most independent signal (max |rho|=0.23); cross-family mutation (IOPV x depth) has 'far higher marginal value than more imbalance variants'.

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: queue_refill_asym_300s
prototype.mechanism: Coarse resiliency / queue-refill asymmetry: after a top-of-book depth depletion step on one side, how much depth is back 15s later, averaged over depletion events in the trailing 300s, bid vs ask, normalized by average top-of-book size. A bid queue that refills faster than the ask queue means patient buy-side liquidity keeps re-arming: downward probes get absorbed and the next move is biased up (fast refill = temporary impact = mean reversion of the depleting move; slow/partial refill = informed consumption = continuation). This is a genuine DYNAMICS quantity - refill speed - orthogonal to depth-imbalance LEVELS (the oir/wdi family).
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'arrival/cancel dynamics only testable via snapshot-delta reconstruction' on SSE and the opportunity map lists resiliency as unexplored depth-side; Obizhaeva & Wang (2013) resiliency after large trades; Foucault-Kadan-Kandel (2005) limit order book replenishment.

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: rv_asym_300s
prototype.mechanism: Directional accumulation of volatility over minutes: the library rv_60s/rv_300s keep only the MAGNITUDE of realized variance, but volatility clusters with a sign signature -- runs of downside jumps (stop cascades, distressed/inventory selling) vs upside jumps (short covering, news absorption). The trailing-300s realized semivariance asymmetry (up-RV minus down-RV over total) is a signed vol-state: asymmetric vol regimes persist (vol-of-vol clustering) and carry directional drift into the next minutes, whereas pure vol level is direction-free. Targets 300s/900s, exactly where the unsigned rv_60s is the only library factor whose |IC| RISES with horizon.
prototype.inspiration: Realized semivariance and good/bad volatility: Barndorff-Nielsen, Kinnebrock & Shephard (2010), Patton & Sheppard (2015, REStat). Digest iter-000: rv_60s |IC| rises monotonically 0.014@15s -> 0.047@900s (vol information lives in the minutes window) but the library keeps it unsigned; vol-of-vol/second-moment accumulation is the lens item, made directional via semivariance asymmetry (an unsigned vol-of-vol level was rejected ex ante as direction-symmetric and not worth a trial-ledger entry).

prototype.name: session_clock
prototype.mechanism: Intraday session-clock seasonality: maps each snapshot to its elapsed continuous-trading time in [0,1] (09:30->0, 11:30->0.5, 13:00->0.5, 15:00->1), skipping the lunch break. This is the clean test of whether 588000 short-horizon returns carry any deterministic time-of-day drift (open/close effects, lunch-resumption, U-shape positioning). Pure calendar/time features have no microstructure state of their own, so a null result is informative: seasonality must enter as CONDITIONING of other signals, not as a standalone directional factor.
prototype.inspiration: digest: 'GAP dimension = time_of_day (ts_ms unused by all 12 factors - open/close auctions, lunch-break boundary, U-shape vol normalization, time-conditioning)'; docs/knowledge/02 section 6 intraday seasonality (U-shape volume/vol, 13:00 second open).

prototype.name: ti_accum_300s
prototype.mechanism: Persistence of signed-volume asymmetry over minutes: the library trade_imbalance_60s is a 60s snapshot of directional flow that decays to zero IC by 300-900s, but informed flow is worked into price over MANY minutes as one-sided meta-orders (Kyle 1985), and the price impact of executed flow decays only as a power law (~t^-1/2, Bouchaud et al. 2004). A trailing 300s average of signed trade imbalance is an ACCUMULATION state variable: it keeps the direction of persistent one-sided flow while averaging out idiosyncratic bursts, matching the minutes-scale memory a 60s window cannot see. Targets the 300s/900s horizon gap.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'FLOW SIGNALS DIE BY 900s ... long-horizon flow constructs need accumulation/state variables instead of 60s windows'; 300s horizon = 0/12 stage1 passes, the biggest open gap. Accumulation logic analogous to VPIN's bucketed signed-volume sums (Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara 2012) applied to the exchange-aggressor-flagged imbalance; impact power-law tail per Bouchaud, Gefen, Potters & Wyart (2004).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: ti_ewm_accel_120s
prototype.mechanism: Aggressive-flow acceleration: fast EWMA (15s half-life) minus slow EWMA (60s half-life) of signed trade imbalance - a MACD of aggressor flow. The LEVEL of imbalance says where flow has been; the acceleration says where it is turning. A burst of one-sided aggression (sweeping several book levels within seconds) precedes short-horizon continuation (queue depletion cascades), while a deceleration of previously strong flow precedes stalls/reversion. Because it is a difference of two backward filters of the same series it is nearly orthogonal to the flow LEVEL factors by construction.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: flow signals die by 900s and peak at 15s - the fresh information in flow is its CHANGE, not its level; momentum-trigger logic in order-flow bursts (Cartea-Jaimungal-Penalva 2015, ch.8 aggressive-order dynamics).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: ti_ewm_state_300s
prototype.mechanism: Flow-accumulation state variable: an exponentially-weighted running integral of signed aggressive trade imbalance with ~150s half-life. Meta-orders (institutional execution, arbitrage baskets vs IOPV) arrive over minutes, so the integrated imbalance of executed aggressor flow is a persistent pressure/information state, not a 60s impulse. High positive state = sustained net buying aggression accumulated over the last several minutes -> continuation expected at 60-300s horizons, where the library's fixed 60s windows have already decayed to their tails.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: '300s HORIZON = WEAKEST AND MOST OPEN ... every library flow factor uses a 60s lookback, so 300s only sees decay tails. Proposals with 2-5 min state variables (flow accumulation) directly target this gap'; meta-order propagation and square-root impact (Bouchaud-Gefen-Potters-Wyart 2004, G(t) ~ t^-1/2).

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: trade_arrival_burst
prototype.mechanism: Trade-arrival bursts (Hawkes self-excitation / ACD): information events make trading cluster in time, so a burst in the arrival rate relative to its trailing baseline flags the START of an information episode that then unfolds over minutes. Unlike ofi/trade_imbalance (signed direction of flow) this is direction-free INTENSITY: a burst says 'something is happening', and on 300/900s horizons the continuation of the episode (in both volatility and drift of the already-revealed direction) should be forecastable. Complements the size-blind flow sums with a timing signal; iter-001 established the mechanism was untestable without trade counts -- n_trades_60s was materialized exactly to unblock it.
prototype.inspiration: Engle & Russell (1998) ACD; Hawkes (1971) self-excitation; iter-001 candidates.json needs_materialization entry (accumulation-regime lens); digest: arrival dynamics only testable via snapshot-delta reconstruction on SSE -- now available as an engine column.

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: vol_adj_slope
prototype.mechanism: Volatility-adjusted book slope: a steep order book partly just encodes that recent volatility has been low (book_slope corr ~0.60 with rv_300s). A causal trailing-window regression removes the vol-explained component, leaving the slope deviation NOT explained by recent realized vol -- the pure book-shape / support-resistance concentration signal that carries minutes-scale (300s+) predictive content, targeting the open 300s gap.
prototype.inspiration: digest: 'book_slope correlated with rv_300s (rho=0.60): on 588000 slope partly just encodes recent volatility; a vol-adjusted slope is an obvious mutation' + '300s horizon = weakest and most open'.

reasons: no horizon passed (need IS |t| >= 2.0, OOS |t| >= 2.0, retention >= 0.5 with same sign)

prototype.name: wdi_mom_90s
prototype.mechanism: Momentum of book state: the LIBRARY tests only the LEVEL of weighted depth imbalance (wdi), the slowest-decaying signal on 588000 (half-life 900s). A book that is actively BUILDING one-sided depth over the last ~90 seconds is a different state from one that is statically lopsided: the delta separates active accumulation of book pressure (queue being rebuilt on one side) from stale imbalance that market makers have already priced. Rising wdi momentum should precede continued mid drift at 60-300s horizons, adding the time-derivative dimension of the depth family that the level-only library lacks.
prototype.inspiration: Digest iter-000: wdi is the cost-friendly champion with the slowest decay (still IC 0.134/t=4.4 at 900s); opportunity map lists depth DELTA as unexplored; queue-imbalance changes as the coarse direction of net queue replenishment (cf. Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014 OFI book-event decomposition); lens item 'momentum-in-book-state'.
